name: multi_device_scene
description: Create a new scene/group -- or add members to an existing one -- in a single call, given a list of member devices with controller/responder roles. Prefer this over repeated group_scene_op add_member calls whenever the customer describes a scene/group as a whole (e.g. 'make a scene where keypad 1 and keypad 2 are controllers and the dimmer is a responder'). A device can only be a controller in ONE scene at a time -- if a requested controller is already a controller elsewhere, this call rejects up front with an error naming that existing scene, before touching anything. That is a real, permanent constraint, not a transient/server error -- never retry with the same or a guessed different address for that device (e.g. swapping a keypad button's address for the keypad's main/primary address, or vice versa) hoping it works, and never remove it from its existing scene without asking first. Tell the customer plainly which scene the device already controls and ask how to proceed (a different device, or explicit confirmation to remove it from that scene first via group_scene_op remove_member) -- and consider whether they identified the wrong device to begin with.

group_address.description: Real id of an existing scene/group to add these members to, exactly as shown in DEVICE DATABASE. Omit to create a new scene/group.

group_name.description: Name for the new scene/group when group_address is omitted. Omit to let NuCore assign one automatically.

devices.description: Non-empty list of member devices to add, each with its role in the scene.

link_address.description: The device's real id, exactly as shown in DEVICE DATABASE.

role.description: Whether this device triggers the scene (controller) or reacts to it (responder).

name.description: Optional display name for this member within the scene.
